title: Input error laws with the same moments reverse Gaussian area changes in six USGS landslide maps
abstract: We test how the input error law changes nonlinear mean affected area in six archived USGS landslide maps. We keep the latent mean and SD recovered in a prior audit. Gaussian propagation reproduces area ratios of 1.42 to 2.59 relative to plug-in estimates. Explicit error laws with the same mean, SD and median give ratios of 0.9917 to 0.9943 in all six cases. These examples put 0.005% probability near 141 SD and are not proposed physical error models. A constructive proof shows that moments alone do not identify the direction of the change for a bounded increasing transform. Finite-support optimization gives attainable ranges under added support and symmetry assumptions. All tested grid laws bounded by 3 SD raise the mean, and symmetric grid minima stay above one out to 32 SD. These grid ranges are not certified continuous-support bounds. The result limits an inference from moments; it does not refute the earlier conditional Gaussian calculation or test observed landslide calibration. Code, 96 error-law witnesses, aggregate results, exact input hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Gaussian and rare-tail laws with the same latent mean, SD and median give opposite area changes. Finite-support grid ranges show the effect of added support assumptions. These are model comparisons, not observed calibration.

citations.reason: Uses the six selected archived files, provenance and latent-scale interpretation; reproduces its conditional Gaussian totals and tests other moment-matched laws.
Operational uncertainty verification motivates testing assumptions in downstream hazard products.
